description: Comprehensive question bank derived from FDA/SDA Computer Knowledge - Digital Technology PDF. Covers all topics: Digital Technology Fundamentals, Cloud Computing, Digital Payments, UPI, Online Banking & EFT, E-commerce, E-governance, Digital Signatures, Digital Certificates & PKI, Indian Digital Institutions, Digital Safety & Fraud Prevention, and High-Yield Comparisons. Questions are structured for KEA examination preparation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is digital technology?

options.A: Technology that uses continuous analogue signals only
options.B: Electronic systems that represent, process, store and transmit information using discrete values, commonly binary digits 0 and 1
options.C: Technology used only for telephone communication
options.D: A system that uses only mechanical components

questions.explanation: Digital technology uses electronic systems that represent, process, store and transmit information using discrete values, commonly binary digits 0 and 1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is digital data?

options.A: Information represented in a form that digital devices can process, store or transmit

questions.explanation: Digital data is information represented in a form that digital devices can process, store or transmit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is digitisation?

options.A: The use of digital technologies to transform processes
options.B: The conversion of information from an analogue or physical form into a digital form, such as scanning a paper document
options.C: A broader organisational change through digital technologies
options.D: The process of storing data only on paper

questions.explanation: Digitisation is the conversion of information from an analogue or physical form into a digital form, such as scanning a paper document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is digitalisation?

options.A: The conversion of analogue information into digital form
options.B: The use of digital technologies to improve or transform processes, services and activities
options.C: A broader societal change in how value is delivered
options.D: The process of scanning paper documents

questions.explanation: Digitalisation is the use of digital technologies to improve or transform processes, services and activities.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is digital transformation?

options.A: The conversion of physical documents into digital files
options.B: The use of digital technologies to improve existing processes
options.C: A broader organisational or societal change in how services, operations and value are delivered through digital technologies
options.D: The process of installing new software

questions.explanation: Digital transformation is a broader organisational or societal change in how services, operations and value are delivered through digital technologies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an analogue signal?

options.A: A signal represented using discrete binary values 0 and 1
options.B: A signal that varies continuously over time and can take a range of values
options.C: A signal used only in computers
options.D: A digital signal with only two values

questions.explanation: An analogue signal varies continuously over time and can take a range of values.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital signal?

options.A: A signal that varies continuously over time
options.B: A signal that can take any value in a range
options.C: A signal represented using discrete values, commonly binary 0 and 1
options.D: A signal used only in analogue telephones

questions.explanation: A digital signal is represented using discrete values, commonly binary 0 and 1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a bit?

options.A: A group of 8 bits
options.B: A binary digit; the smallest unit of digital information, with a value of 0 or 1
options.C: A unit of storage equal to 1024 bytes

questions.explanation: A bit is a binary digit; the smallest unit of digital information, with a value of 0 or 1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a byte?

options.A: A single binary digit

questions.explanation: A byte is a group of 8 bits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital platform?

options.A: A hardware device used for printing
options.B: A software-based environment that enables users, organisations or services to interact, exchange information or conduct transactions
options.C: A physical market for buying goods

questions.explanation: A digital platform is a software-based environment that enables users, organisations or services to interact, exchange information or conduct transactions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is information and communication technology (ICT)?

options.A: The technologies used to create, process, store and communicate information, including computers, networks, software and telecommunications

questions.explanation: ICT refers to the technologies used to create, process, store and communicate information, including computers, networks, software and telecommunications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an online service?

options.A: A service delivered only through physical offices
options.B: A service delivered or accessed through a network, usually the Internet
options.C: A service that uses only analogue signals
options.D: A service available only on paper

questions.explanation: An online service is a service delivered or accessed through a network, usually the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is interoperability?

options.A: The ability of a single system to operate independently
options.B: The ability of different systems, organisations or applications to exchange information and use it meaningfully
options.C: The process of converting analogue to digital

questions.explanation: Interoperability is the ability of different systems, organisations or applications to exchange information and use it meaningfully.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital identity?

options.A: A physical identity card
options.B: A set of electronic attributes or credentials used to represent and authenticate a person or entity in digital environments

questions.explanation: A digital identity is a set of electronic attributes or credentials used to represent and authenticate a person or entity in digital environments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital transaction?

options.A: A transaction that uses only cash
options.B: A transaction initiated, processed or recorded using electronic systems
options.D: A transaction recorded only on paper

questions.explanation: A digital transaction is a transaction initiated, processed or recorded using electronic systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital ecosystem?

options.A: A natural environment with digital devices
options.B: A connected environment of people, organisations, technologies, platforms and services that interact digitally

questions.explanation: A digital ecosystem is a connected environment of people, organisations, technologies, platforms and services that interact digitally.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud computing?

options.A: Computing that uses only local hardware
options.B: The delivery of computing resources and services, such as servers, storage, databases, networking and software, over a network on demand
options.C: A type of weather prediction technology
options.D: Computing that requires physical servers in every office

questions.explanation: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing resources and services, such as servers, storage, databases, networking and software, over a network on demand.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main benefit of cloud computing?

options.A: It requires users to own all infrastructure
options.B: It provides flexible access to computing resources without requiring users to own and maintain all the underlying infrastructure
options.C: It eliminates the need for networks
options.D: It only works for large organisations

questions.explanation: The main benefit of cloud computing is that it provides flexible access to computing resources without requiring users to own and maintain all the underlying infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is on-demand self-service in cloud computing?

options.A: A user must contact the provider for every resource request
options.B: A user can provision computing resources when needed, usually without requiring direct human interaction with the service provider
options.C: A service that is available only during business hours
options.D: A service that requires physical installation

questions.explanation: On-demand self-service means a user can provision computing resources when needed, usually without requiring direct human interaction with the service provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is resource pooling in cloud computing?

options.A: A cloud provider shares pooled computing resources among multiple customers while logically separating their workloads and data
options.B: A single customer uses all resources exclusively
options.C: Resources are stored only on local devices
options.D: Resources are allocated manually by the customer

questions.explanation: Resource pooling means a cloud provider shares pooled computing resources among multiple customers while logically separating their workloads and data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is rapid elasticity in cloud computing?

options.A: The inability to change resources
options.B: The ability to scale cloud resources up or down quickly in response to demand
options.C: The process of physically moving servers

questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity is the ability to scale cloud resources up or down quickly in response to demand.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is measured service in cloud computing?

options.A: Cloud usage is monitored and measured, often allowing providers to charge according to consumption
options.B: A service that is free of charge
options.C: A service that cannot be measured
options.D: A service that charges a fixed fee regardless of usage

questions.explanation: Measured service means cloud usage is monitored and measured, often allowing providers to charge according to consumption.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main cloud service models?

options.A: Public, private and hybrid
options.B: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS) and Software as a Service (SaaS)

questions.explanation: The main cloud service models are Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS) and Software as a Service (SaaS).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)?

options.A: A cloud model that provides ready-to-use software applications
options.B: A cloud model that provides fundamental computing resources such as virtual machines, storage and networking, while the customer manages much of the software stack
options.C: A cloud model that provides only a development platform
options.D: A cloud model that provides only email services

questions.explanation: IaaS is a cloud model that provides fundamental computing resources such as virtual machines, storage and networking, while the customer manages much of the software stack.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Give an example of an IaaS service.

options.A: Web-based email
options.B: Virtual machine and storage services offered by providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud

questions.explanation: Virtual machine and storage services offered by providers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud are examples of IaaS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Platform as a Service (PaaS)?

options.A: A cloud model that provides fundamental computing resources
options.B: A cloud model that provides ready-to-use software applications
options.C: A cloud model that provides a managed platform and tools for developing, testing, deploying and running applications
options.D: A cloud model that provides only storage

questions.explanation: PaaS is a cloud model that provides a managed platform and tools for developing, testing, deploying and running applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Software as a Service (SaaS)?

options.A: A cloud model in which users access a provider-managed software application over a network, commonly through a browser or app
options.B: A cloud model that provides virtual machines
options.C: A cloud model that provides only networking resources
options.D: A cloud model that requires users to manage the underlying infrastructure

questions.explanation: SaaS is a cloud model in which users access a provider-managed software application over a network, commonly through a browser or app.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Give examples of SaaS applications.

options.A: Virtual machines and storage
options.B: Web-based email, online office applications, customer relationship management systems and cloud-based collaboration tools

questions.explanation: Web-based email, online office applications, customer relationship management systems and cloud-based collaboration tools are examples of SaaS applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main cloud deployment models?

options.A: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS
options.B: Public cloud, private cloud, community cloud and hybrid cloud

questions.explanation: The main cloud deployment models are public cloud, private cloud, community cloud and hybrid cloud.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a public cloud?

options.A: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation
options.B: Cloud infrastructure made available to multiple customers over a network and operated by a cloud provider
options.C: Cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common requirements
options.D: Cloud infrastructure that combines private and public clouds

questions.explanation: A public cloud is cloud infrastructure made available to multiple customers over a network and operated by a cloud provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a private cloud?

options.A: Cloud infrastructure available to multiple customers
options.B: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation, though it may be managed internally or by a third party
options.C: Cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common requirements
options.D: Cloud infrastructure that combines private and public clouds

questions.explanation: A private cloud is cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation, though it may be managed internally or by a third party.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a community cloud?

options.A: Cloud infrastructure available to the general public
options.B: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation
options.C: Cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common requirements, such as security, policy or compliance needs
options.D: Cloud infrastructure that combines private and public clouds

questions.explanation: A community cloud is cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common requirements, such as security, policy or compliance needs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hybrid cloud?

options.A: Cloud infrastructure available only to the public
options.B: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organisation
options.C: An arrangement that combines private or on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and applications to move or work across environments
options.D: Cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common requirements

questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud is an arrangement that combines private or on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and applications to move or work across environments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud storage?

options.A: A service that stores data on local hard drives only
options.B: A service that stores data on remote infrastructure and allows authorised users or applications to access it over a network
options.D: A type of cloud computing service model

questions.explanation: Cloud storage is a service that stores data on remote infrastructure and allows authorised users or applications to access it over a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Give examples of cloud storage services.

options.A: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox and Apple iCloud

questions.explanation: Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Dropbox and Apple iCloud are examples of cloud storage services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud backup?

options.A: A backup copy of data stored on local drives only
options.B: A backup copy of data stored on cloud infrastructure for recovery in case of loss, corruption or device failure
options.D: A type of cloud deployment model

questions.explanation: Cloud backup is a backup copy of data stored on cloud infrastructure for recovery in case of loss, corruption or device failure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file synchronisation in cloud services?

options.A: The process of deleting files from all devices
options.B: The process of keeping selected files or folders consistent across multiple devices or cloud locations
options.C: The process of converting files to analogue format
options.D: The process of storing files on physical media

questions.explanation: File synchronisation in cloud services is the process of keeping selected files or folders consistent across multiple devices or cloud locations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud scalability?

options.A: The inability to change resources
options.B: The ability to increase or decrease computing resources to meet changing workloads
options.C: The process of physically moving servers

questions.explanation: Cloud scalability is the ability to increase or decrease computing resources to meet changing workloads.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a virtual machine (VM)?

options.A: A physical computer
options.B: A software-based computer that runs an operating system and applications using virtualised computing resources

questions.explanation: A virtual machine (VM) is a software-based computer that runs an operating system and applications using virtualised computing resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is virtualisation?

options.A: The creation of physical versions of computing resources
options.B: The creation of virtual versions of computing resources, such as servers, storage, networks or operating systems
options.C: The process of converting analogue to digital
options.D: A type of cloud deployment model

questions.explanation: Virtualisation is the creation of virtual versions of computing resources, such as servers, storage, networks or operating systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cloud data centre?

options.A: A facility containing servers, storage, networking and supporting infrastructure used to provide cloud services
options.B: A type of cloud storage service

questions.explanation: A cloud data centre is a facility containing servers, storage, networking and supporting infrastructure used to provide cloud services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cloud region?

options.A: A geographical area in which a cloud provider operates one or more data centres
options.B: A type of cloud service model

questions.explanation: A cloud region is a geographical area in which a cloud provider operates one or more data centres.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cloud availability?

options.A: The degree to which a cloud service is operational and accessible when users need it

questions.explanation: Cloud availability is the degree to which a cloud service is operational and accessible when users need it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a service-level agreement (SLA) in cloud computing?

options.A: A formal agreement defining service expectations and measurable commitments, such as availability, support or performance
options.C: A type of cloud deployment model

questions.explanation: An SLA in cloud computing is a formal agreement defining service expectations and measurable commitments, such as availability, support or performance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multi-tenancy in cloud computing?

options.A: An architecture in which a single customer uses all resources
options.B: An architecture in which multiple customers share underlying resources while their data and workloads are logically isolated

questions.explanation: Multi-tenancy in cloud computing is an architecture in which multiple customers share underlying resources while their data and workloads are logically isolated.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the risks of cloud computing?

options.A: Only hardware failure
options.B: Risks include misconfiguration, account compromise, data breaches, service outages, vendor dependency, privacy issues and inadequate backup or access controls

questions.explanation: Risks of cloud computing include misconfiguration, account compromise, data breaches, service outages, vendor dependency, privacy issues and inadequate backup or access controls.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does storing a file in the cloud automatically make it secure?

options.A: Yes, cloud storage is always secure
options.B: No. Security depends on provider controls, account protection, encryption, sharing permissions, configuration and user practices
options.C: Yes, if the file is large
options.D: Yes, if the file is encrypted by the provider

questions.explanation: No. Security depends on provider controls, account protection, encryption, sharing permissions, configuration and user practices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the shared responsibility model in cloud computing?

options.A: A model in which the cloud provider is responsible for all security
options.B: A model in which the customer is responsible for all security
options.C: A model in which the cloud provider and customer each have defined security responsibilities; the division varies by service model and provider
options.D: A model in which no one is responsible for security

questions.explanation: The shared responsibility model is a model in which the cloud provider and customer each have defined security responsibilities; the division varies by service model and provider.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital payment?

options.A: A payment made using physical cash
options.B: A payment in which money is transferred or a payment instruction is processed electronically rather than by exchanging physical cash
options.C: A payment made only through cheques

questions.explanation: A digital payment is a payment in which money is transferred or a payment instruction is processed electronically rather than by exchanging physical cash.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main advantage of digital payments?

options.A: They require physical cash
options.B: They can make transactions faster and more convenient while providing electronic transaction records
options.C: They are only available during business hours
options.D: They eliminate the need for banks

questions.explanation: The main advantage of digital payments is that they can make transactions faster and more convenient while providing electronic transaction records.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Name common digital payment methods in India.

options.A: UPI, debit cards, credit cards, internet banking, mobile banking, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, prepaid payment instruments and Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)

questions.explanation: Common digital payment methods in India include UPI, debit cards, credit cards, internet banking, mobile banking, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, prepaid payment instruments and Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cashless transaction?

options.A: A transaction completed using physical cash
options.B: A transaction completed without physical cash, using an electronic or other non-cash payment method
options.C: A transaction completed using cheques only

questions.explanation: A cashless transaction is a transaction completed without physical cash, using an electronic or other non-cash payment method.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a contactless payment?

options.A: A payment made by inserting a card into a terminal
options.B: A payment made by bringing a compatible card, phone or wearable device near a payment terminal, commonly using NFC or another contactless technology
options.D: A payment made through a cheque

questions.explanation: A contactless payment is a payment made by bringing a compatible card, phone or wearable device near a payment terminal, commonly using NFC or another contactless technology.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment gateway?

options.A: A physical door used for payments
options.B: A technology service that securely captures and routes payment information between a merchant, payment processor and relevant financial institutions

questions.explanation: A payment gateway is a technology service that securely captures and routes payment information between a merchant, payment processor and relevant financial institutions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment aggregator?

options.A: A regulated or authorised service provider that enables merchants to accept payments through one or more payment methods and settles funds according to its arrangement

questions.explanation: A payment aggregator is a regulated or authorised service provider that enables merchants to accept payments through one or more payment methods and settles funds according to its arrangement.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Point of Sale (POS) terminal?

options.A: A device or system used by a merchant to accept and process customer payments, often by card or contactless methods

questions.explanation: A POS terminal is a device or system used by a merchant to accept and process customer payments, often by card or contactless methods.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a QR code payment?

options.A: A payment made using cash
options.B: A payment initiated by scanning a Quick Response code that contains or identifies payment information
options.C: A payment made through a cheque
options.D: A payment made using a credit card

questions.explanation: A QR code payment is a payment initiated by scanning a Quick Response code that contains or identifies payment information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a static QR code?

options.A: A QR code that generally contains fixed merchant or payment details, with the payer entering or confirming the amount
options.B: A QR code generated for a particular transaction
options.C: A QR code that changes with every transaction
options.D: A QR code used only for websites

questions.explanation: A static QR code generally contains fixed merchant or payment details, with the payer entering or confirming the amount.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a dynamic QR code?

options.A: A QR code that contains fixed merchant details
options.B: A QR code generated for a particular transaction and commonly containing transaction-specific details such as the amount or reference
options.C: A QR code used only for websites
options.D: A QR code that never changes

questions.explanation: A dynamic QR code is generated for a particular transaction and commonly contains transaction-specific details such as the amount or reference.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a debit card?

options.A: A payment card that allows the cardholder to borrow up to an approved credit limit
options.B: A payment card that typically draws funds directly from the cardholder's linked bank account
options.C: A card that stores prepaid value
options.D: A card used only for ATMs

questions.explanation: A debit card is a payment card that typically draws funds directly from the cardholder's linked bank account.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a credit card?

options.A: A payment card that draws funds directly from the cardholder's bank account
options.B: A payment card that allows the cardholder to borrow up to an approved credit limit and repay the amount under the issuer's terms
options.C: A card that stores prepaid value
options.D: A card used only for ATM withdrawals

questions.explanation: A credit card is a payment card that allows the cardholder to borrow up to an approved credit limit and repay the amount under the issuer's terms.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a prepaid payment instrument (PPI)?

options.A: A payment instrument in which value is stored in advance and used to make payments, subject to applicable rules
options.B: A payment card linked to a bank account

questions.explanation: A prepaid payment instrument (PPI) is a payment instrument in which value is stored in advance and used to make payments, subject to applicable rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a digital wallet?

options.A: A physical wallet
options.B: An application or service that stores payment credentials or prepaid value and enables electronic payments

questions.explanation: A digital wallet is an application or service that stores payment credentials or prepaid value and enables electronic payments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is NFC?

options.A: Near Field Communication, a short-range wireless technology used for contactless communication and payments

questions.explanation: NFC stands for Near Field Communication, a short-range wireless technology used for contactless communication and payments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment switch?

options.A: A physical switch used to turn on payment devices
options.B: A system that routes electronic payment transactions between participating institutions or payment networks

questions.explanation: A payment switch is a system that routes electronic payment transactions between participating institutions or payment networks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a transaction reference number?

options.A: An identifier assigned to a payment or transaction that helps users and institutions trace it

questions.explanation: A transaction reference number is an identifier assigned to a payment or transaction that helps users and institutions trace it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment settlement?

options.A: The process through which funds are transferred and financial obligations between parties are completed
options.B: The process of initiating a payment
options.C: The process of cancelling a payment
options.D: The process of storing payment data

questions.explanation: Payment settlement is the process through which funds are transferred and financial obligations between parties are completed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment reversal?

options.A: A transaction process in which a previously debited or processed payment is reversed or returned, depending on the payment system and circumstances

questions.explanation: A payment reversal is a transaction process in which a previously debited or processed payment is reversed or returned, depending on the payment system and circumstances.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a chargeback?

options.A: A reversal of a card transaction initiated through the cardholder's issuing bank under applicable card-network rules

questions.explanation: A chargeback is a reversal of a card transaction initiated through the cardholder's issuing bank under applicable card-network rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a failed digital payment?

options.A: A payment attempt that does not complete successfully, although the account may sometimes show a temporary debit pending reconciliation

questions.explanation: A failed digital payment is a payment attempt that does not complete successfully, although the account may sometimes show a temporary debit pending reconciliation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a user do if money is debited but the digital payment shows failed?

options.A: Ignore the issue
options.B: Check the transaction status and reference number, wait for the applicable reversal or settlement period, and contact the bank or payment provider through official channels if unresolved
options.C: Immediately share the UPI PIN with the bank
options.D: Install a remote access app from an unknown caller

questions.explanation: The user should check the transaction status and reference number, wait for the applicable reversal or settlement period, and contact the bank or payment provider through official channels if unresolved.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a merchant?

options.A: A person or business that sells goods or services and accepts payment from customers

questions.explanation: A merchant is a person or business that sells goods or services and accepts payment from customers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a payment confirmation?

options.A: A notification or record indicating the reported status of a payment; users should verify the transaction in the official bank or payment app

questions.explanation: A payment confirmation is a notification or record indicating the reported status of a payment; users should verify the transaction in the official bank or payment app.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does UPI stand for?

options.A: Unified Payments Interface

questions.explanation: UPI stands for Unified Payments Interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is UPI?

options.A: A physical payment card
options.B: UPI is an instant payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) that enables interoperable bank-to-bank payments through supported applications

questions.explanation: UPI is an instant payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) that enables interoperable bank-to-bank payments through supported applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which organisation developed UPI?

options.A: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

questions.explanation: UPI was developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is NPCI?

options.A: National Payments Corporation of India, an organisation that operates and develops retail payment and settlement systems in India

questions.explanation: NPCI is the National Payments Corporation of India, an organisation that operates and develops retail payment and settlement systems in India.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which institution regulates payment systems in India?

options.A: NPCI
options.B: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), under the applicable legal and regulatory framework

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulates payment systems in India under the applicable legal and regulatory framework.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: When was UPI launched?
questions.explanation: UPI was launched in 2016.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a UPI ID or Virtual Payment Address (VPA)?

options.A: A payment address used to identify a UPI user or account for sending or receiving payments without sharing the bank account number and IFSC in every transaction
options.B: A physical address of a bank branch

questions.explanation: A UPI ID or Virtual Payment Address (VPA) is a payment address used to identify a UPI user or account for sending or receiving payments without sharing the bank account number and IFSC in every transaction.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a UPI PIN?

options.A: A password for email
options.B: A confidential personal identification number used to authorise specified UPI transactions from a linked bank account

questions.explanation: A UPI PIN is a confidential personal identification number used to authorise specified UPI transactions from a linked bank account.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Should a user share a UPI PIN with anyone?

options.A: Yes, with bank staff
options.C: No. A UPI PIN must remain confidential and should never be shared with another person
